blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At the executive level, the gap between profit and cash is one of the most useful signals available. A healthy business generates cash roughly in line with its reported profits. A business whose cash persistently lags its profit is doing one of a few things — growing working capital faster than sales, recognising revenue before it is collected, capitalising expenses that should have been booked, or, in the worst cases, producing profits that have no real money behind them.

None of these is necessarily dishonest, and each deserves a specific conversation. Growing working capital may be the cost of fast expansion — good in the right context, dangerous in the wrong one. Early revenue recognition may be correct under the rules but aggressive in spirit. Capitalisation may be appropriate, or simply a way of pushing expenses into the future.

If the senior team had not been tracking the gap, the warning would have arrived later, louder and far more expensive. That is why the best leaders watch it every month, in quiet, steady conversations nobody outside the room ever sees.

items.q: According to the text, what makes the profit-cash gap valuable to executives?
options: It is one of the most useful early signals available
It replaces the need for an audit
items.why: "the gap between profit and cash is one of the most useful signals available".

items.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as a reason cash may lag profit?
options: Capitalising expenses that should have been booked
Growing working capital faster than sales
Recognising revenue before it is collected
items.why: Corte de pessoal não está na lista — os itens são capital de giro, receita antecipada, capitalização e lucros sem dinheiro real.

items.q: The phrase "correct under the rules but aggressive in spirit" suggests that…
options: something can be technically legal yet stretch the intent of the rules
items.why: Inferência: "aggressive in spirit" indica que algo cumpre a letra da norma mas força seu espírito.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A widening profit-cash gap always signals fraud
Tracking the gap early lowers the eventual cost
The gap deserves a specific conversation for each cause
A healthy business converts profit into cash
items.why: Inferência: o texto insiste que "none of these is necessarily dishonest" — atribuir fraude a todo caso contraria o argumento.

items.q: What does the line about the warning arriving "later, louder and far more expensive" imply?
options: The finance team should stay silent
Cash flow is irrelevant to strategy
Ignoring the gap makes the eventual reckoning worse
items.why: Inferência: monitorar cedo evita que o problema exploda mais tarde de forma mais cara — daí o acompanhamento mensal.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver na reunião do comitê executivo. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
I want to flag something on the group company before it becomes a headline. Over the last four months, profit has held up nicely, but cash conversion has quietly drifted the other way. I am not making an accusation — I want us to have the conversation now, while it is still cheap to have.

When I pulled the numbers apart, most of the gap traces back to working capital. Receivables are stretching, and a slice of it is revenue we have booked but not yet collected. On its own, that could simply be the cost of a fast expansion — perfectly defensible. But if the trend held for another two quarters without collection catching up, I would want a very different explanation from the team.

So here is what I am proposing. Each month, alongside the profit line, we review one number: how much of that profit actually turned into cash. If the two move together, wonderful, we move on. If they keep separating, we ask why, calmly, before anyone outside this room ever notices. That is the whole point of watching it early — the warning stays quiet, steady, and ours to manage.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why is Oliver raising the issue now?
options: To have the conversation while it is still cheap to have
To cut the group company's budget
To formally accuse the finance team
To announce it publicly to shareholders
items.why: "I want us to have the conversation now, while it is still cheap to have."

items.q: Where does most of the gap trace back to, according to Oliver?
items.why: "most of the gap traces back to working capital. Receivables are stretching…"

items.q: What would make Oliver want "a very different explanation"?
options: The trend continuing two more quarters without collection catching up
A change in the audit firm
items.why: "if the trend held for another two quarters without collection catching up, I would want a very different explanation".

items.q: What can we infer about Oliver's attitude toward the team?
options: He gives them the benefit of the doubt while staying watchful
He wants to escalate to the board immediately
He is indifferent to the outcome
He assumes wrongdoing from the start
items.why: Inferência: ele diz que não é acusação e admite que o desvio pode ser defensável, mas quer monitorar de perto.

items.q: What is the main advantage of watching the gap early, in Oliver's view?
options: It removes the need for monthly reporting
The warning stays quiet and manageable inside the room
It guarantees the profit will rise
items.why: Inferência: "the warning stays quiet, steady, and ours to manage" — o controle permanece interno e barato.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Cash generation should stay roughly in line with reported profit." In line with means…
items.why: In line with = alinhado a, coerente com.

items.q: "For three months, collections have lagged our sales." To lag means to…
items.why: To lag = ficar atrás, atrasar-se em relação a algo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The accounting is legal, but the timing is ___ in spirit."
items.why: Aggressive = agressivo; força o limite da norma sem necessariamente violá-la.

items.q: "They chose to capitalise the costs rather than expense them." To capitalise means to…
options: record a cost as an asset instead of an immediate expense
items.why: To capitalise = capitalizar: registrar como ativo em vez de despesa imediata, empurrando o custo para o futuro.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The best leaders watch the number every month, in quiet, ___ conversations."
items.why: Steady = constante, regular — o oposto do alarde reativo.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em reuniões de finanças. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Let's keep an eye on the cash-conversion number each month." To keep an eye on means to…
items.why: Keep an eye on = monitorar de perto, acompanhar.

items.q: "None of this will move the needle unless receivables come down." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, causar diferença perceptível.

items.q: "Two committee members pushed back on the early-warning framing." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The CFO still needs to sign off on the revised revenue policy." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "The team agreed to tighten collections but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.
